items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So I think that might be what he was referring to, I can not be one hundred percent, but that Latino tinge, what this author referred to, that’s what he was talking about.

ctx.x: And it talks a lot about the Caribbean influence. [scats] It has like what they called that cincio rhythm [scats] you could put it in clave. A lot of it has the [scats] that’s the cincio. [scat] It’s five notes. Cincio means cinco and that music came to New Orleans. And a lot of it came via Mexico, I didn’t know that, that there was like a family of teachers that came through New Orleans to teach and they were very influential in the early development of jazz, which I never knew.
